prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim. Injury: back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1163; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection. Insured vehicle was stopped at the light when struck from behind by the third-party vehicle. Police report requested. Both drivers reported no visible damage to the front of the insured vehicle beyond the bumper area. Photos of both vehicles uploaded to file.

Entry 2: Third-party carrier acknowledged liability coverage review. Claimant's vehicle sustained rear damage and airbag was not deployed. Claimant reports neck and lower back discomfort at scene and was transported to urgent care for evaluation. Diagnosis noted as lumbar strain with soft tissue involvement. Medical records requested.

Entry 3: Notice of representation received. Claimant is now represented by counsel, and all further communication is to be directed to counsel's office. Letter of representation placed in file. Recorded statement from claimant will be scheduled through counsel only. Reserve reviewed and adjusted to reflect bodily injury exposure.

Entry 4: Medical records received from urgent care and primary care provider. Records document lumbar strain, prescribed muscle relaxants and a course of physical therapy referral. No prior back complaints noted in the last five years of records. Counsel has submitted a demand package requesting review. File referred to bodily injury unit for evaluation.

Entry 5: Physical therapy progress notes reviewed. Claimant has completed the initial evaluation and is attending sessions twice weekly, with reported gradual improvement in range of motion. Counsel advised that treatment is ongoing. Claim remains open pending completion of treatment and receipt of final billing. Diary set for follow-up with counsel.
